answer: Agents could earn influence only through a bonded reputation: each identity locks scarce tokens, and its weight grows slowly as peers verify useful work across independent tasks. If an identity is exposed as a duplicate or submits provably conflicting results, the bond is slashed and its accumulated standing erased. A farm can still create many names, but cannot multiply influence for free; it must tie up capital in every name and risk losing it. Even a saffron garden proposal at a summit gains no extra weight from a swarm of fresh accounts.
